AC-2 The explanation is visible without hovering or expanding anything.
AC-3 The four deviation values render exactly as they do today, in the same neutral tone.
AC-4 Nothing in the tab offers or implies inspection, extraction, download or decryption of an archive.

report.objective: Stop a digest-level verdict reading like an inspection. A Gaia system backup archive is opaque: the product compares two of them by digest alone and can say only that the bytes differ. The device's Backup tab shows that verdict as `unchanged` or `changed` with no indication of how it was reached, so an operator reasonably reads it as the product having looked inside. Record 14I DV-3 requires the product to say so rather than imply it inspected the contents.
output_contract: An operator knows what the backup verdict is based on, and is not left believing the product looked inside.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One explanatory line on a surface that already exists; the constraint is the wording, not the markup.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
The two frontend commands run from ui2/frontend; the privacy gate runs from the repository root.
Run only the commands named above. Do not run the Java build.
Run `git diff --check origin/main` before every commit and fix what it names.
Leave the worktree clean: write reports outside the repository or remove them before closing.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is only for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the pull request or code comments.
Commit early and often on your lane.
The SESSION_CLOSE quotes the wording you chose and says where it is placed.
risks: Writing the explanation as a warning, which turns an honest limitation into an apparent fault.
Hiding it behind a hover, where the reader who most needs it never sees it.
Wording it so it reads as a promise that a future version will look inside.

in: The Backup tab says, where the verdict is shown, that a backup archive is compared by digest alone -- so unchanged means the bytes are identical and changed means they are not, and neither is a statement about what is inside.

Say it once, where it is needed, in the product's own voice. A column heading, a short note under the table, or an explanation attached to the verdict are all acceptable; a tooltip alone is not, because it is invisible to a reader who does not hover.
Keep every deviation value neutral in tone. This movement adds an explanation, not an alarm.
Tests: the explanation is present when the list has rows; it does not appear as an error or a warning; the existing rendering of the four values is unchanged.
out: Any attempt to inspect an archive, open it, or derive structure from it. The archive is opaque and this movement's whole point is to say so.
Any change to the API, the deviation vocabulary, or the CHECK constraint.
Any change to the configuration side's structural summary.
Any artefact byte, path, download link or decrypt affordance.
Restyling the existing chips or introducing a tone that reads as a fault.
